document: Task 1 test-preservation inventory and replacement map
scope: Playwright specs under agent-control-tower/act-dashboard/e2e/ plus the LangChain/Python-dependent Java and CI test entry points that the cutover/removal tasks (T17-T20) affect. This is an inventory with replacement mapping, not a whole-repo test census.
rule: A spec or test entry may only be removed on cutover when its business purpose is carried by the mapped replacement. Credential-gated or disabled cases are listed explicitly in disabledOrGated; every retained business purpose there must land in a runnable deterministic replacement.
notes: Case-count rule (recount performed mechanically on 2026-09-23, fix round B, with a node script over the `path` values below): a `cases` value counts Playwright case declarations in the spec file text - a bare `test('...')` or a modifier declaration `test.skip('...')` / `test.fixme('...')` / `test.fail('...')` / `test.only('...')` / `test.slow('...')` whose first argument is a string literal, at any nesting depth. Cases inside `test.describe` and `test.describe.skip` suites are counted; a whole-file `test.describe.skip` makes every case in the file a disabled case but still counts it. Suites (`test.describe`, `test.describe.configure`) and hooks (`test.beforeEach/afterEach/beforeAll/afterAll`, `test.use`, `test.step`, `test.extend`) are not case declarations, and a runtime `test.skip(condition, '...')` inside a case body does not add a case. Recount total across the 62 specs: 245 case declarations; 15 entries disagreed with their previous value and were corrected.

t19FixRound3.familyA_nativeAskLookup: DECIDED (contract-accurate lookup; no assertion weakened): a NATIVE permission ask is correlated with its RUN, not with a kanban card. PermissionCoordinator.register writes acp_permission_requests.run_id plus Approval.runId and sets no kanbanItemId (only the gate path does: KanbanReviewAskCreator sets kanbanItemId on the REVIEW_REQUEST ask). core-permissions.spec.ts therefore resolves the native ask by run: dispatchAsk dispatches the card, reads the pickup-written linkedRunId (/kanban/items/{id}) and resolves the run PENDING native ask through fixtures.pendingRunApprovals plus a filter that excludes the gate-path review ask (askType REVIEW_REQUEST / no optionsJson). The card path (/approvals?kanbanItemId=, helper cardLinkedAsks) is kept as the GATE-ask path and is used to assert the two contracts are distinct (the native ask is never returned by it and carries kanbanItemId null). The fixtures now pin the peer scenario deny-write (one native edit permission offering exactly proceed_once/cancel) instead of a scenario that raises no ask at all, and each dispatched run owns a DIRECT workspace the spec observes for the gated fixture write.
t19FixRound3.familyA_denialRePin: RE-PINNED with the contract evidence (design V4 / peer suite: denial produces no side effect; the T12 verdict reason is the coordinator decision text): the denial case still asserts the ask is DENIED and now asserts the exact recorded verdict ("Operator denied Write (native permission request 0)"), that the gated edit never appears in the run admitted workspace, and that the run reaches its own core outcome (COMPLETED - the deny-write fixture reports the decision window). The retired ADK task-gate semantics (a denied task gate cancelled the run) do not exist for core-owned runs; nothing in the coordinated native-ask contract cancels a run on a denial.
t19FixRound3.familyA_deliveryWire: REAL PRODUCTION GAP FOUND AND FIXED AT THE ROOT: PermissionCoordinator.decide returned the native reply for the owning session and both production callers (REST ApprovalController, MCP ApprovalTools) dropped it, so a decided ask never reached the core and the core kept waiting (a decided-but-undelivered ask is indistinguishable from no decision at the peer). New seam io.aria.conductor.execution.approval.PermissionReplySink (functional, resolved lazily through ObjectProvider to break the coordinator construction cycle): CoreExecutionService implements it (deliver -> the run own session; no session in this process -> reported and dropped, never routed elsewhere) and CoreRuntimeConfiguration binds the sink bean to the coordinator. RED captured by disabling the hand-off (PermissionCoordinatorTest.allowOnceDecisionIsHandedToTheOwningSessionSinkExactlyOnce fails), GREEN with it; the held (manual pause) path keeps its single delivery through deliverHeldDecisions and is pinned not to double-deliver.
t19FixRound3.familyB_pausePremise: RE-PINNED to the contract that genuinely holds a prompt, with the T7 evidence: the opencode pause-resume prompt completes by design - the peer suite pins the immediate DONE response and only the writer survives (peer-actions.test.mjs:1377-1382) and scenarios.json declares no held message for it, while the qoder pause-resume prompt stays open until the session is cancelled (peer-actions.test.mjs:967) and the message is held until the decision exactly for the opencode git-push gate (scenarios.json). The pause case is therefore pinned to qoder + pause-resume: RUNNING is observed first (pollUntil), the held prompt native ask is granted exactly once (grantRunAsks, still asserting grant count > 0 and uniqueness), the owned writer ticks.log is observed in the run admitted workspace, pause freezes the bytes for 3 s, resume grows them, cancel ends exactly CANCELLED. The workspace-diff assertions of the old case are observed directly on the admitted workspace bytes: the route reads the engine legacy per-run scratch directory (WorkspaceManager.getIfExists(runId)), not the run admitted workspace, so its content assertions were never satisfiable for a governed run; the route own contract stays covered by core-workspaces.spec.ts.
t19FixRound3.familyB_harnessPauseWire: HARNESS WIRE FIXED: the bridge protocol has no pause RPC (it refuses with E_PAUSE_UNSUPPORTED), which the production qoder session passes through as an unverified acknowledgement, so a qoder harness run could never be paused even though the harness declares BACKEND_SUSPEND and serves pause/resume as verified process-tree suspension for the opencode core. CoreE2eQoderAdapter now wraps the production session in SuspendableSession, which answers pause/resume with the harness process transport (CoreE2eProcessBackend.State.pausePeer/resumePeer) and delegates everything else (sessionId/prompt/decide/cancel) to the production session.
